tagline.text: A Spanish-era church begun in 1614 in a northwestern Cagayan coastal town

location.label: Location
location.text: Centro, Pamplona, Cagayan (behind the municipal hall, along Manila North Road)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (around the town fiesta on April 29)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 1–2 hours (half a day with the town)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~2,000 (church visit and local transport, per person)

children.text: Pamplona Church is the Saints Peter Martyr and John Nepomucene parish church in the center of Pamplona, Cagayan. Construction began in 1614, it is counted among the oldest churches in Cagayan, and it was declared a National Historical Landmark in 1939.

The official name of Pamplona Church is the Saints Peter Martyr and John Nepomucene Parish Church. It stands in Centro, Pamplona, on the northwestern coast of Cagayan, and is still an active parish church under the Archdiocese of Tuguegarao. It was originally called the Church of Masi. Because Pamplona was formed in 1842 by merging the two villages of Abulacan and Masi, the church's roots go back to the Masi village era, well before the town took its present name.

According to several sources, construction began in 1614 under Fr. Miguel Martin de San Jacinto and was finished in 1617. However, one source says no exact completion date appears in history books, and another gives a span running to 1627, so the exact year cannot be stated with certainty. Many articles call it "the oldest church in Cagayan," but Wikivoyage's more cautious wording, "one of the oldest churches in Cagayan," is the safer way to put it. The National Historical Commission of the Philippines (NHCP) declared the church a National Historical Landmark in 1939.

The church was damaged by an earthquake in 1721 and was repaired by Fr. Jose Caño. In the 1970s it fell into ruin, and only the walls and facade remained. In 1982 parishioners formed a group to seek support and funds for restoration, the cornerstone was laid on July 6, 1990, and Archbishop Diosdado Talamayan rededicated the church on April 29, 1993. The church you see today is a restoration that kept the surviving old walls and facade. One blog describes the facade as a darker crimson than other Cagayan churches, with a distinctive arch at the entrance.

Pamplona is far from Manila and also more than 140 km from Tuguegarao, the center of Cagayan, so it is not a place most ordinary travelers pass through. It does lie on the way toward Ilocos Norte, which makes it a good stop on a tour of Cagayan's old churches or on an overland trip linking Cagayan and Ilocos. Rather than expecting a flashy tourist spot, think of it as a quiet visit to a church more than 400 years old and a small coastal town, and you are more likely to be satisfied. The town's history is also long. Wikipedia says Salcedo's 1572 expedition to explore Cagayan began at the mouth of the Pamplona River, and that when the two villages merged in 1842, the Dominican Fr. Pedro Montenegro named the town after his hometown of Pamplona in Spain. Knowing this background helps explain why such a large church stands in the middle of the town. Looking around the church takes an hour or two, but allow half a day if you also want to see the town market and the river mouth.

blocks.title: One of the oldest churches in Cagayan

children.text: A Spanish-era church whose construction began in 1614, it is a fixture of old-church pilgrimages in northern Cagayan. Together with St. Raymond de Peñafort Church in Rizal, Cagayan, it is also counted among the oldest churches still standing in Cagayan.
The NHCP declared it a National Historical Landmark in 1939. The wording of any marker at or inside the church may change over time, so please check it on site.

It collapsed in the 1970s until only its walls and facade remained, then parishioners raised funds, the cornerstone was laid in 1990, and it was rededicated in 1993. It is fun to tell apart the surviving old walls and facade from the restored parts.

blocks.title: A dark crimson facade and entrance arch

children.text: One travel blog says the facade is a darker red than other Cagayan churches and that the arch at the entrance is distinctive. Photos work best in the morning or late afternoon when the light is low and angled.

blocks.title: A church standing on a large rock

children.text: One source says the church was built on a huge rock formation, which helped it survive the centuries. The figures given for the rock's size differ between sources and are unconfirmed, so treat this description as background only.

blocks.title: Two patron saints and the April 29 town fiesta

children.text: The Pamplona town fiesta is held around April 29 every year and lasts two days, with processions carrying the images of St. John Nepomucene and St. Peter Martyr. The schedule can change from year to year, so check the parish and town announcements.

blocks.title: The Masi River mouth and nearby sights

children.text: The town sits at the mouth of the Masi River, and natural attractions such as Mount Malagabavi in Masi, Pikkan Falls, Isla Paraiso and Millennium Beach are listed within the municipality. You can combine them with a church visit, but check on site how to reach each one.
Arrive in Pamplona Centro and walk to the church behind the municipal hall. The municipal hall and Manila North Road are close, so it is easy to find.
Take your time around the facade, the entrance arch and the restored interior. Stay quiet during Mass and refrain from taking photos.
Stroll through the town market and along Manila North Road to look at nipa palm handicrafts and snacks.
Have lunch at a restaurant near the market. If you have not chosen one in advance, pick a place that is busy with locals.
If you have time, hire a tricycle to see the Masi River mouth. Agree on the fare and the duration with the driver first.
The church itself takes about an hour to see, but check in advance when you need to head back to Tuguegarao or Laoag, because of public transport schedules.
Leave Tuguegarao and head northwest, stopping at old churches along the road one by one. Decide beforehand which churches you will visit.
Have lunch around Abulug. Pamplona is still some distance ahead.
Arrive at Pamplona Church, look at the facade and interior, and read about its restoration.
Before dark, move on to your lodging or head back toward Laoag or Tuguegarao.
Pamplona is about
650km
from Manila, a town on Manila North Road (the national highway).
Long-distance buses and vans from Manila toward Tuguegarao or Laoag use this road. Wikivoyage says buses, vans and minibuses from Metro Manila heading to Junction Luna also serve Pamplona.
Check the exact drop-off point and schedule with the bus company in advance.
It is too far to reach in a single day from Manila, so an overnight stop along the way is recommended.
One option is to fly from Manila to Tuguegarao Airport (TUG) and continue overland. Whether flights operate varies by season, so check with the airline.
From Tuguegarao to Pamplona is about
140km
, and Wikivoyage says it takes roughly 3 to 5 hours from Tuguegarao or Laoag.
Tricycles are the main means of transport within the town.
The church is in Centro behind the municipal hall, so it can also be reached on foot from the market and Manila North Road.
Pamplona has a tropical climate, with average temperatures generally between 23 and 29°C. Annual rainfall is about 1,664 mm, with December the wettest month and April the driest.
Visiting the church is easier in the dry season when the roads are dry. Around April 29 the town fiesta is held, and you can see the processions of the two patron saints.

There is not much lodging in town. Wikivoyage lists a beach resort in Nagattatan, but check rates and booking methods yourself. If you need a larger place to stay, you can also stay in Laoag or Tuguegarao and visit on a day trip.

Pamplona Public Market is along Manila North Road and is a good place to buy a simple meal and snacks. Handicrafts made from nipa palm from the Masi River mouth and nipa spirits are known as local specialties. Choose long-established eateries near the market, and check whether you can carry specialty goods before buying them. From the town center you can walk to the church, so you do not need to rent a car. Restaurant information changes over time, so check on site, and rather than fixing on a named place in advance, we suggest walking once around the market and then choosing. Bring enough food and water for your schedule.
The church is still a parish church, so stay quiet during Mass and dress modestly.
Check visiting hours and Mass times on the parish Facebook page or on site.
It is far from both Tuguegarao and Laoag, so arrange your return transport in advance.
During the April 29 fiesta it is crowded, so book lodging and transport early.
The facade photographs best in the morning or late afternoon when the sunlight is angled.
Bring plenty of cash. You cannot assume an ATM is always available in town.
If you plan to visit natural attractions such as Mount Malagabavi or Pikkan Falls, ask at the town tourism office. The tourism office is said to be at the municipal hall on Bayot Street.
In summer, bring a hat, water and sunscreen.
Since the church is right behind the municipal hall, it is convenient to ask the tourism office there first about the latest events and visiting information.
We could not confirm the church's visiting hours or entry conditions. Ask the parish or the municipal tourism office before you go.
On a long trip, if you miss the last public transport, it is hard to find lodging.
In the rainy and typhoon seasons, travel on the national highway can be delayed, so check the latest weather advisories.
The nearest hospitals are said to be in Abulug and Sanchez Mira, so bring basic medicines.
Taking photos inside the church or moving around during Mass can be disrespectful, so be careful.
The phrase "oldest church" and the completion year vary between sources, so treat them as a guide only.

from Pamplona by road. It has the airport and many places to stay, and serves as a base for this area.

blocks.title: Masi River mouth and Isla Paraiso

children.text: Floating cottages are said to be available for rent at the river mouth among the nipa groves in town. Check on site how to use them.
A long gray-sand beach running from the Masi mouth toward Sanchez Mira. Check locally whether swimming is possible.
